Question Choices: If P(A) = 0.3, P(B) = 0.6, and A and B are mutually exclusive, find P(A or B).
Hints: Mutually exclusive means no overlap.|Add the probabilities.
Solution: Add P(A) and P(B), then subtract the overlap P(A and B), which was counted twice. Mutually exclusive events have zero overlap. Here 0.3+0.6 = 9/10.

Question Choices: If P(A) = 0.7, what is P(not A)?
Solution: An event and its complement exhaust the possibilities and cannot both occur. Thus P(not A)=1-P(A). Here 1-0.7 = 3/10.

Question Choices: Two independent events have P(A) = 0.5 and P(B) = 0.2. Find P(A and B).
Solution: For independent events, P(A and B)=P(A)P(B). Independence is the assumption that permits multiplication of the two unconditional probabilities. Here 0.5*0.2 = 1/10.

Question Choices: A fair die is rolled once. Find the probability of rolling a 3 or a 5.
Solution: Add P(A) and P(B), then subtract the overlap P(A and B), which was counted twice. Mutually exclusive events have zero overlap. Here 1/6+1/6 = 1/3.

Question Choices: If P(A) = 0.6, P(B) = 0.5, and P(A or B) = 0.9, find P(A and B).
Hints: Rearrange the addition rule.|P(A and B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A or B).
Solution: Rearrange the addition rule: P(A and B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A or B). Here 0.6+0.5-0.9 = 1/5.
